clue.text: The French support party, Republican, in region of Canada

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French
a bra is an undergarment that supports
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A French-speaking political group is said to be backing a Republican party somewhere in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Labrador is the mainland part of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador.

clue.text: Departed, not on time

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both deceased (the late president) and tardy (a late train).

clue.text: Biscuit or drink popular in the US

definitions.meaning: a British chocolate sandwich biscuit with a creamy filling
an American whiskey distilled mainly from corn

explanation.definitionFit: Bourbon is both a British chocolate cream biscuit and a corn-based American whiskey.

clue.text: Recognise a Conservative has awareness

parts.note: awareness of something is knowing about it

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that a Tory politician is well informed.
explanation.definitionFit: To recognise someone's point or presence is to admit or accept it openly; synonyms.

clue.text: Working towards the same goal against team

parts.note: on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A player cooperates with teammates while facing an opposing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' is the less obvious sense of ON, as in propped on the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being onside means being in agreement and supporting the same aims as others.

clue.text: Information about opening in Loire Valley

indicators.note: about means the information word goes around the other letter

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of Loire

explanation.surface: Tourist facts about the start of a trip through the Loire Valley.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; 'about' puts it around L, the first letter of Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Gain knowledge of Shakespearean king close to Regan

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, here of Regan

explanation.surface: A student studies King Lear's relationship with his daughter Regan.
explanation.walkthrough: Regan is one of Lear's daughters in the play, which keeps the surface tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to acquire understanding or information about it; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Knight and son seen dancing? How absurd

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the letters of son and seen are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight and his son caught dancing would be a ridiculous spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the silly scene; 'Knight' is N as in chess notation, not K.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'Nonsense!' dismisses something as ridiculous, as does 'How absurd'.

clue.text: Rabbit's head found in food wagon

indicators.note: found in means one letter sits inside the food word

parts.note: tuck is British schoolboy slang for food, especially sweets and snacks

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of Rabbit's

explanation.surface: A rabbit's head turns up in a food delivery wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: TUCK is British slang for snacks, as in a school tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A truck is a goods vehicle, and in railway use an open wagon.

clue.text: Suffer in South American train, right away

parts.note: US means American, as in US citizens

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out of train

explanation.surface: A traveller endures a gruelling ride on a South American train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R from TRAIN, leaving TAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain an injury or loss is to undergo or experience it.

clue.text: Calm about drop, an unexpected piece of good luck

indicators.note: about means the calm word is placed around the drop word

parts.note: calm as a noun is tranquillity or peacefulness
a dip is a drop or fall, as in a dip in prices

explanation.surface: Staying calm when things drop turns out to be a lucky break.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipity is the happy occurrence of fortunate events by chance.

clue.text: Gondola bore exotic citrus fruit

indicators.note: exotic means strange or unusual, so these letters are rearranged into something unfamiliar

explanation.surface: A Venetian gondola is carrying an unusual cargo of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges the letters of GONDOLA and BORE.
explanation.definitionFit: This variety of orange has red-streaked flesh, so it is a kind of citrus.

clue.text: Alphabetical list in article editor finally put in magazine

indicators.note: put in means these letters are placed inside the magazine word

parts.note: a glossy is a magazine printed on shiny paper
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of editor

explanation.surface: An editor finally agrees to include an alphabetical index in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places AR (A plus the R ending editor) inside GLOSSY.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical list of terms with their meanings, usually at the back of a book.

clue.text: Friendless individual living initially in outskirts of Londonderry

indicators.note: in means the other letters sit inside the outer pair
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters, here of Londonderry

parts.note: one means a single individual

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of living

explanation.surface: A solitary person lives on the edge of Londonderry, a city in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE plus L (start of living) goes inside L and Y, the ends of Londonderry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lonely is without companions; friendless is a close synonym.

clue.text: Relatives legally joining son

parts.note: in law means according to the law, legally
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A family's relatives become connected through a legal marriage to a son.
explanation.walkthrough: IN LAW is read as the phrase meaning 'legally'.
explanation.definitionFit: In-laws are relations by marriage, such as a spouse's parents.

clue.text: A permit secured by the gymnast, perhaps

indicators.note: secured by means the permit word is held inside the word the

parts.note: to let is to permit, as in let me go

explanation.surface: A gymnast is granted a permit to compete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a piece of the wordplay, not a link word, and 'secured by' signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast is one example of a sportsperson, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Spent energy on fine garden party

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a fete is an outdoor fundraising event, often held in a garden

explanation.surface: Someone used up all their energy at a lovely garden party.
explanation.walkthrough: A FETE is a British outdoor fair raising money for a church or school.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete can mean worn out and exhausted, no longer vigorous, which matches spent.

clue.text: Rugby halfback is hard, unfriendly

parts.note: the stand-off is the fly-half, one of the two halfbacks in rugby union
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough rugby player is described as hard and unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the stand-off (or fly-half) plays just behind the scrum-half; both are called halfbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standoffish is cold and distant towards others, aloof.

clue.text: Beggars once covering this crime

indicators.note: the phrase Beggars once covers, or holds within it, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Beggars of old were blamed for a particular crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' signals letters held inside begg(ARS ON)ce.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Actual field of interest limited

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the last letter of the field word is dropped

parts.note: a realm is a field or domain of activity or interest

explanation.surface: Someone's true area of expertise is quite narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' cuts the final M from REALM.
explanation.definitionFit: Real and actual both mean existing in fact rather than imagined.

clue.text: Basic US rate confused English

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up, so US rate is rearranged

explanation.surface: An American basic tax rate baffles the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges US RATE into AUSTER, followed by E.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means plain and without luxury, close in sense to basic or spartan.

clue.text: Girl showing anger, one having lost face

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger

indicators.note: losing its face means the word one drops its front letter

explanation.surface: A girl shows her temper and loses face in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost face' removes the first letter from ONE, leaving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female given name, and crosswords often define names by 'girl'.

clue.text: Pull domesticated ox round rear of barn

indicators.note: round means the ox word goes around the other letter

parts.note: a yak is a long-haired ox domesticated in Tibet

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter, here of barn

explanation.surface: A farmer hauls a domesticated ox round the back of the barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps YAK around N, the end of barn.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to give a sudden hard tug, which is a pull.

clue.text: Extremely healthy? I agree

definitions.meaning: in excellent health, fit as a fiddle
a phrase of consent, like all right then

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase reads literally as in excellent health and idiomatically as an expression of assent.
